title: Certified release workflow YAML registration safety

phases.objective: Keep the certified Production release-cut validation workflow parseable and registrable while preserving its fail-closed title gate and read-only authority.

e2e_journeys.actor: GitHub Actions workflow registrar and repository reviewer
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: The certified release-cut workflow is loaded from the pull-request candidate tree.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Both title-gated jobs use complete quoted YAML scalars, the registration and convergence contracts reject the unsafe unquoted form, and no write or Production authority is introduced.
steps: Load the candidate workflow and locate the validation and finalize job conditions.
Verify that each startsWith title condition is wrapped as one quoted YAML scalar.
Run both the focused registration contract and the composed Production promotion convergence contract.
Reject an unquoted condition containing the release title prefix and colon-space sequence.
Confirm the workflow remains pull_request_target based with contents read permission and no PR comment write path.
assertions: The certified-release-cut-ci condition is quoted as a complete YAML scalar.
The finalize condition is quoted as a complete YAML scalar.
The focused registration contract rejects both unsafe unquoted title-condition forms.
The canonical Production promotion convergence contract requires the same quoted governed eligibility selector.
The workflow retains read-only contents permission and does not introduce write, deployment, migration, provider, credential, runtime, or secret authority.

phases.objective: Expose a canonical parser-registration diagnostic when GitHub rejects a future workflow revision before job creation.
Prove the registration contract across synchronized pull requests, reruns, and default-branch updates without weakening fail-closed behavior.
This repository workflow registration repair has no provider or live-runtime canary authority.
This repair grants no Production merge, deployment, migration, provider, credential, or secret authority.
